M1 bring-up package — generic VESA linear-framebuffer display driver (vmdisp9x)
Purpose: prove the Win9x display-driver stack works on the T61 BEFORE any
NVIDIA-specific code. This uses the G86's VESA/VBE video BIOS, not native code.

Files: vesamini.vxd, vesamini.drv, vmdisp9x.inf  (built from source, Open Watcom)

Install on the T61 (Windows 98 SE):
  1. Copy all three files to the T61 (e.g. C:\VESADRV\).
  2. First, in Safe Mode, remove the current NVIDIA display adapter entry in
     Device Manager so it stops trying the broken NVCORE path, and set the
     display to "Standard Display Adapter (VGA)". Reboot to a VGA desktop.
  3. Control Panel > Display > Settings > Advanced > Adapter > Change >
     Have Disk > point to C:\VESADRV\vmdisp9x.inf.
  4. Choose the "VESA VBE 2.0+" entry. Finish, reboot.
  5. Expected: desktop comes up through the VESA framebuffer at a higher
     resolution/colour depth than plain VGA. Note which resolutions are offered.

If it does NOT work, capture: the exact error, whether VGA still works, and
BOOTLOG.TXT. A failure here is about the display stack, not NVIDIA — good to
know before M2/M3.

This is reversible: fall back to Standard VGA in Safe Mode at any time.
